pull_request.title: Magnet System: redesign separated toroids and schematic muon stations
pull_request.head: codex/issue105-separated-toroids
pull_request.body:
The previous barrel toroid overlaps the endcap toroid span and its stronger field target lacks a credible NbTi winding margin. Refs [issue #105](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/issues/105).

This DRAFT design amendment shortens the barrel coils to **12 m**, lengthens each endcap to **6 m**, and provides **0.80 m between their complete warm axial envelopes**, retaining the **3 T central solenoid**. A thinner homogeneous pack and freshly solved currents give about **0.48 T at the two ordinary intercoil reference points**. The sampled exterior maximum rises from **3.50 T to 3.64 T** under higher-order checks; the approximately **4 T conductor limit remains an unresolved engineering requirement**, rather than a certified bound. Complete vacuum self/mutual energy and global 30 MJ/m³ cold-volume closure are recomputed.

Three nested schematic station pairs extend the outer chambers through the transition. On the same 134,400-direction bank they provide **84.06% three-station geometric availability by solid angle within |eta|<3** (83.80% within 3.5), versus **62.79%** (62.59%) for shortening every barrel chamber. This is a continuous-shell ceiling before finite panels, supports and services; eta3.5 stretch coverage remains unmet. The joint direct field, signed bending diagnostics and angular refinement are retained; no new interpolation map or production geometry is installed.

- [Design, source rationale and open interfaces](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/issue105-separated-toroids/docs/design/inputs/DES-039-issue105-separated-toroids.md)
- [Drawing, results, reproducibility and limits](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/issue105-separated-toroids/docs/validation/DES-039/issue105/README.md)
- [Separate physics assessment, adverse findings and fixes](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/issue105-separated-toroids/docs/validation/DES-039/issue105/physics-review.md)

**Validation:** 33 focused analytic/field/energy/sizing controls pass, including stationwise barrel-or-wheel counting and ray-batch invariance. Source hashes, project/session records and token-site validation/build pass. SysArch and MuonTech supplied separate interface/placement assessments; PhysVal independently checked the numerical claims and counting corrections.

Stacked on PR87's branch containing merged PR90. Earlier maps, 936 detailed panels, frames and DD4hep validation remain historical. Continuous-pack peak field, NbTi operating margin, tiny cold support allowance, nonlinear HCAL energy, forces/quench, an accessible middle-station cryostat volume and finite-panel/material transport require review. DES004/DES039/DES040 remain DRAFT; no human sign-off or production integration.

issues.title: Magnetic Field: Review Toriodal magnet System
issues.body:
This is an expert review comment from @mgtmentink: 

" 
- Looking at the 3 T solenoid, it looks reasonable.
- The Toroid on the other hand looks, at first glance, very problematic. With Nb-Ti conductor technology, which is used for large superconducting detector magnets, you cannot go well beyond ~4 T on the superconducting windings. Given how inefficient Toroid coils are, for the ATLAS  Toroid this ~4 T limit gives a typical field of 0.5-1.0 T between the coils (depending where you are looking, also see attached simulation). With that in mind, going to 2-3 T as proposed here looks infeasible. One may imagine a new technology that goes beyond the limits of Nb-Ti, but I wouldn't count on it, and even if feasible it would be very risky and would cost an absolute fortune (>> 1 BCHF)
- The other thing about the Toroid option is that it seems like Barrel and End-Cap Toroid coils are interleaved (unlike the ATLAS ones where the Barrel Toroid and End-Cap Toroid coils occupy different volumes). Given the Lorentz force interaction between the coils, this looks mechanically very problematic.

To summarize, the solenoid seems to be okay, but the Toroid is unfeasible. For the Toroid, I would suggest to consider more or less the same field as generated by the ATLAS Toroid, and to forget about interleaving the Barrel and End-Cap Coils. What may be interesting is to keep the End-Cap Toroid coils of similar size but make the Barrel Toroid coils much shorter (such that the End-Cap-Toroid and Barrel Toroid no longer occupy the same space), which is an option that we previously considered for FCC-hh.
"

Please re-design the magnetic field along side the suggestion: 
- no interleave of Barrel EC toroid
- shorter barrel, longer endcaps 
- strength limitations as described

Then make a possible schematic chamber placement suggestion, keeping a 3 -chamber coverage as high as possible.


**Some resources**:
[ATLAS Superconducting Magnets model description_11-7-24.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34137942/ATLAS.Superconducting.Magnets.model.description_11-7-24.pdf)

Explicit generic-agent role instructions were prepared and read; native profile
loading is not claimed. /root/sysarch (I105-SysArch) independently checked PR87
fe372194038ed2af9617c27defffba09ae6d683f, PR90db88f594ab29a2a509b4308fdfddf14ffe5f822e,
PR9452922c71a58a4d799abeccc716a716fa2ba52521, and the updatedcae3 merge.
It recommended the12m/6m hosts, derived0.8m warm separation, and identified
S2-vessel, rear support, coil-force and HCAL/service interfaces.

/root/muontech (I105-MuonTech) checked the same revisions and identified
full-depth transition inequalities, orthogonal host separation, distinct-station
counting, finite-aperture stretch loss, and the need to repack actual chambers.
The coordinator selected wheel radii6.1/7.5/9m and lengths6.4456/10/13.8m
using those inequalities. The different schematic shell model cannot be directly
ranked against the historical936-panel results.
